report_name: 1Password Discloses Security Breach; Customer Vaults Safe

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Actor
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actor responsible for the 1Password breach, who compromised an employee's GitHub account to access backend systems, inject malicious code, and exfiltrate customer administrative data.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attacker gained initial access to 1Password's backend systems by using the compromised credentials of an employee's GitHub account.

attack_patterns.name: Hijack Execution Flow
attack_patterns.description: The attacker pushed malicious code to 1Password's backend services after gaining access to private source code repositories, hijacking the normal execution flow to exfiltrate data.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The malicious code injected by the attacker executed on 1Password's backend infrastructure and downloaded a subset of customer administrative data.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Identified as a potential follow-on attack, where attackers could use the stolen customer names and email addresses to craft targeted phishing campaigns to trick users into revealing their account passwords or Secret Keys.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.description: The attacker compromised an employee's GitHub account to access private source code repositories and push malicious code to 1Password's backend services.

identities.name: 1Password
identities.description: A password management provider whose backend systems were compromised via a developer's GitHub account. The company reported that customer vault data remained secure due to its zero-knowledge architecture.

indicators.name: Forced Git Push to Protected Branch
indicators.pattern:
title: Forced Git Push to Protected Branch
id: 7c5a1b9e-8d4f-4e2a-9b1c-0f3d5a7b6c8d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects a 'git push --force' command, which can be a sign of a malicious code injection that bypasses review processes, as mentioned in the 1Password breach analysis.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/1password-hacked-customer-data-and.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-26
tags:
  - attack.t1574
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/git'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'push'
      - '--force'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of 'git push --force', which can indicate an attempt to overwrite repository history and inject malicious code, bypassing normal pull request and review workflows.

relationships.source_name: Forced Git Push to Protected Branch
